projects.name: Khidma - Service Marketplace Platform
projects.context: Personal project, published on GitHub as separate frontend, backend and mobile repositories
projects.pitch: Tunisian home-services marketplace: clients describe a need, compare proposals from verified professionals, and follow the intervention from booking to completion.
projects.problem: Finding a reliable home-service professional is fragmented and hard to coordinate from the first request to the final intervention.
projects.solution: One platform centralizing service discovery, client requests, professional proposals, appointment tracking, notifications and private conversations.
projects.role: Designed and built end to end: React/TypeScript web app, React Native/Expo mobile app, modular Fastify API, MongoDB data model and CI/CD.
highlights: Client, professional and admin roles with JWT access + refresh tokens, email OTP verification, password reset and refresh-token revocation.
MongoDB transactions accept a proposal atomically and prevent duplicate professional assignments.
Persisted real-time notifications with Socket.IO and private Stream Chat conversations linked to requests and proposals.
Privacy by design: exact addresses and contact details stay hidden until the appointment is confirmed; access is controlled by role and business status.
GitHub Actions CI for the mobile app: ESLint, TypeScript validation, Expo Web build and dependency security audit (npm audit).
Automated Docker image builds published to GitHub Container Registry (GHCR), with Nginx serving the Expo Web app.
Tested with Vitest and MongoDB Memory Server; API documented with Swagger/OpenAPI.

projects.name: VELOR - Cinematic Cafe Site & Dashboard
projects.pitch: Scroll-driven brand site for a fictional Paris coffee bar (Velvet Cold Coffee), paired with an admin dashboard for orders, menu and opening hours, synced live through a typed mock REST API.
projects.problem: Build a brand experience that feels like a film, scrubbing a 267-frame video as you scroll, without giving up performance, accessibility or real content in the HTML.
projects.solution: Next.js app with two route groups: a GSAP-driven public site and a separate /admin dashboard that never share heavy code (the site never loads the API client, the admin never loads GSAP or frames).
workflow: Guest orders ahead on the site
Lands on the kanban order board
Menu and hours sync back live
projects.role: Designed and built end to end as a solo project: art direction, scroll choreography, data layer, dashboard UI, accessibility and performance tuning, and Vercel deployment.
highlights: Pinned canvas drawing 267 WebP frames tied 1:1 to scroll, streamed progressively (30 up front, the rest when idle); the LCP element is a real <picture> poster.
Typed REST API on MSW v2 with zod as single source of truth, TanStack Query caching/polling, cross-tab sync via BroadcastChannel, optimistic updates with rollback and retry.
Realistic network simulation (300-900 ms latency, failures, timeouts); idempotency keys prevent duplicate orders on retry or double click.
Dashboard: KPIs and Recharts analytics, dnd-kit kanban with full keyboard moves, TanStack Table menu editor with react-hook-form + zod, Ctrl+K command palette.
Accessibility: semantic HTML, keyboard support everywhere, live regions, 44 px touch targets, reduced-motion fallback, axe WCAG 2.1 AA scans with no violations.
results: Lighthouse desktop (production build): Performance 97-98, Accessibility 100, Best Practices 100, SEO 100
CLS of 0 (skeletons reuse the real layout)

projects.name: Specora AI - Idea to Software Specification
projects.pitch: Local-first assistant that turns a rough product idea (typed or spoken) into a reviewable software specification with traceable requirements, user stories and acceptance criteria.
projects.problem: Product ideas start as a paragraph or a voice note; turning them into something precise enough to discuss, test and build is hard.
projects.solution: The LLM proposes a draft; the app normalizes and validates it, and the human reviews assumptions, answers open questions and decides what is ready.
workflow: Traceable requirements, stories and acceptance criteria
highlights: Seven sections in a stable order: overview, functional requirements, user stories, acceptance criteria, non-functional requirements, open questions, assumptions.
The application (not the LLM) owns ID normalization (FR, US, AC, NFR, Q, A) to protect traceability links.
Works with OpenAI or any OpenAI-compatible local LLM endpoint; optional speech-to-text input.
Generation failures are surfaced as actionable errors instead of rendering an invalid draft.

projects.name: AI Detective - Incident Investigation (CLI + Dashboard)
projects.context: Personal project (two repositories: Python core/gateway and React dashboard)
projects.pitch: Turns application logs into evidence-based diagnostic reports and practical developer actions, separating facts from hypotheses.
projects.problem: Reading raw logs line by line is slow, while pasting everything into an LLM gives vague, unsupported answers.
projects.solution: Deterministic parsing and statistics stay the source of truth; a bounded Groq agent with read-only tools proposes causes linked to source line numbers.
workflow: Analyze a log file or connect to a running backend
Parse text / JSON / NDJSON keeping line numbers
Deterministic stats, error groups and timeline
Bounded Groq investigation (+ optional Stack Overflow enrichment)
Markdown / JSON report and copyable resolution prompt
projects.role: Designed and built solo: Python analysis engine, optional FastAPI live gateway, and a separate React/Vite dashboard.
highlights: Core CLI works with no browser, server or LLM; deterministic analysis is the fallback.
Optional FastAPI Live Gateway probes localhost:5000/3000 or a user-given URL and reads text, JSON, NDJSON or stream snapshots.
Separate React dashboard: metrics, every error occurrence with its source line, per-error resolution steps and a structured prompt for one error or the full incident.
Never changes source code or runs arbitrary commands: an investigation assistant, not a black box.
Tested with pytest.
